extracted.intended_audience: advanced users/developers of PARI/GP performing high-precision numerical and algebraic computations
extracted.subtask_description: Documentation of PARI/GP library routines: numerical integration, series/summation/extrapolation methods, product and root finding routines, and data-structure conventions for number fields, algebraic numbers, ideals and related objects. Specifies input formats, assumptions, convergence conditions, performance notes and initialization options.

rubrics_metrics.name: intnumromb: analytic cleanup and singularity conditions for reliable numerical integration
rubrics_metrics.description: For Romberg numerical integration the integrand and its analytic form must have no singularities on the integration interval or at the boundaries; analytical cleanup (e.g. change of variable) must have been done before calling the routine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If integrand has boundary/interval singularities, perform variable changes to remove them. The routine assumes the integrand is well-behaved on [a,b]; otherwise results are unreliable. Use sufficient real precision (example: ~100 bits for ~30 decimal digits).

rubrics_metrics.name: intnumromb: improper integrals and behaviour at infinity
rubrics_metrics.description: For improper integrals (one or both limits ±∞) the function must decrease sufficiently rapidly at infinity; integration by parts or a change of variable is often necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may represent infinity by a large finite number (e.g. 10 for some integrals) but beware of underflow for rapidly decreasing functions — do not use absurdly large constants like 1e1000. Ensure the integrand's tail is within the working precision.

rubrics_metrics.name: intnumromb: integrand magnitude relative to precision
rubrics_metrics.description: The function to be integrated should not be very small (relative to current precision) on the entire interval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If it is uniformly tiny, multiply the integrand by an appropriate constant to avoid underflow/precision loss, then rescale the result.

rubrics_metrics.name: intnumromb: API/syntax and historic variant deprecation
rubrics_metrics.description: Library syntax is intnumromb(void *E, GEN (*eval)(void*,GEN), GEN a, GEN b, long flag, long bitprec). The historical variant using prec in words is obsolete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pass any needed extra data to eval via E (or NULL). Use current signature rather than the obsolete prec-in-words variant.

rubrics_metrics.name: laurentseries: requirement on series valuation
rubrics_metrics.description: laurentseries(f,{M=seriesprecision}, {x=x}) expands f as a Laurent series around x=0 to order M; it requires that f be evaluable on a power series with zero constant term (series valuation == 0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If f cannot be evaluated on series with 0 constant term (valuation != 0) you'll get a domain error. Individual coefficients up to order M can be retrieved with polcoeff(s,i). laurentseries is generally faster and more precise than repeated numeric differentiation (derivnum) for series coefficients.

rubrics_metrics.name: laurentseries: precision and performance notes
rubrics_metrics.description: laurentseries computes f(x + O(x^n)) until n is large enough; resulting series may be more precise than the requested O(x^(M+1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use laurentseries for coefficient extraction and many repeated coefficient computations; examples show it's faster than derivnum for many successive calls.

rubrics_metrics.name: limitnum: assumptions on the sequence and inputs
rubrics_metrics.description: limitnum(expr,{k=20},{alpha=1}) performs Lagrange-Zagier numerical extrapolation on a sequence u_n given either as a closure n->u(n) or a vector. It assumes u_n tends to a finite limit and has an asymptotic expansion in powers of n^{-α}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Routine is purely numerical and heuristic and may fail. If u is passed as a vector it must be long enough (at least k times current realprecision); closures are preferred when feasible. Adjust k and alpha to reflect asymptotic spacing (u(kn) extrapolation) for better results.

rubrics_metrics.name: prod: initialization parameter sets arithmetic type and affects performance
rubrics_metrics.description: prod(X=a,b,expr,{x=1}) computes the product of expr with formal parameter X from a to b. The initialization argument x forces the arithmetic type (integer exact, real with default precision, power series with given O(X^k) precision).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choosing an appropriate x can drastically change running time and memory (examples show degree 5050 vs truncation to O(X^101)). Use specific initializations to ensure operations are done in the desired ring and to improve speed.

rubrics_metrics.name: prodeuler/prodeulerrat/prodnumrat: domain and degree expectations for multiplicative products
rubrics_metrics.description: prodeuler computes product over primes between a and b using eval closure; prodeulerrat/prodnumrat work when the factor functions are rational functions with specified degree constraints (e.g., F a rational function; F-1 rational of degree < 2 for prodnumrat).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure F meets the stated rationality/degree hypotheses; use the specific GEN prodeulerrat/prodnumrat signatures when applicable (they have faster, specialized implementations).

rubrics_metrics.name: prodinf: infinite product stopping criteria and domain requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: prodinf(X=a,expr,{flag=0}) computes an infinite product starting at X=a and stops when relative error of (expression − 1) is less than the default precision; expressions must evaluate to complex numbers. If flag=1 compute product of (1+expr) instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-convergent products will loop indefinitely — be careful to ensure convergence beforehand. Use flag appropriately when expr represents multiplicative increment or when 1+expr is the intended factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: solve (zbrent): bracketing requirement and domain continuity
rubrics_metrics.description: solve(X=a,b,expr) (zbrent) finds a real root in [a,b] using Brent's method under the condition expr(a)*expr(b) ≤ 0 (roots must be bracketed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the function is not defined on the whole [a,b] (e.g., tan(x) on [1,2]) the method can fail or produce errors. Make sure the root interval is valid and the function is continuous/defined everywhere in it.

rubrics_metrics.name: solvestep: heuristic interval-splitting zero-finding and flag meanings
rubrics_metrics.description: solvestep(X=a,b,step,expr,{flag=0}) searches for zeros by naive interval splitting and is heuristic; it may or may not find intended zeros. Flag bits mean: 1 return on first zero found; 2 refine until at least one zero found (may loop if none); 4 multiplicative search (requires a>0 & step>1) else additive; 8 refine until a zero is very close to an integer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use solvestep for exploratory searches; choose flags according to desired stopping behavior; beware infinite loops in refining modes if no zeros exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: sum: finite sum initialization semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: sum(X=a,b,expr,{x=0}) computes a finite sum with initialization x used to force the type of intermediate arithmetic (exact rationals, floating reals at default precision, power series truncated to O(X^k), etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initialization affects performance and result type — e.g., summing 1/i as rationals produces enormous denominators; using floating initialization (0.) is much faster and less memory intensive for numeric approximation.

rubrics_metrics.name: sumalt: alternating series summation assumptions, algorithms and complexity
rubrics_metrics.description: sumalt(X=a,expr,{flag=0}) applies the Cohen–Villegas–Zagier algorithm to (−1)^k a_k alternating series, assuming ak are moments of a positive measure on [0,1] for the flag=0 variant; flag=1 uses a variant with more complicated polynomials. The routine is heuristic; rigorous conditions are difficult to check.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sumalt to guess an infinite alternating sum; if the series already converges geometrically prefer suminf. Complexity for target accuracy 10^{-p} is generally O(p^2) time and space; flag=1 can reduce number of needed terms (n ≈ 0.86p) but has higher overhead (time O(p^3), space O(p^2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: suminf: infinite sum stopping rule and applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: suminf(X=a,expr) sums an infinite series and stops when relative error of the partial sum is less than default precision for 3 consecutive evaluations; terms must be complex numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If series converges slowly, lower realprecision (even 28 digits may be too much) or use specialized summation (sumalt for alternating, sumpos for same-sign terms). Long-running or non-convergent series may hang or require user interrupts.

rubrics_metrics.name: sumnum: Euler–MacLaurin summation hypotheses, precomputation and complexity
rubrics_metrics.description: sumnum(n=a,f,{tab}) numerically sums f(n) from a to +∞ using Euler–MacLaurin, assuming f has positive values and is C^∞; tab (from sumnuminit) precomputes abscissas/weights and asymptotic behaviour, greatly speeding subsequent calls. By default assumes f decreases at least like O(n^{-2}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If f decreases polynomially with exponent −2<α<−1, indicate tab = sumnuminit([+oo,alpha]). If f decreases exponentially indicate tab = sumnuminit([+oo,alpha]) with alpha>0 to avoid exponent overflow. Complexity: f evaluated O(D log D) times where D ≈ realprecision·log(10). Use precomputed tab for repeated high-precision calls. Beware cancellation when evaluating f at huge n — rewrite terms or substitute accurate asymptotic expansions when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: sumnum cancellation warning and remedy
rubrics_metrics.description: sumnum may evaluate f(n) for enormous n (e.g. >1e233), leading to catastrophic cancellation if f's naive formula subtracts large terms to yield small results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rewrite the summand to avoid cancellation or replace f(n) locally by a truncated asymptotic expansion (compute F = truncate(f(1/x)+O(x^k)) and use subst(F,x,1/n) for large n). This can restore full precision.

rubrics_metrics.name: sumnumap (Abel–Plana): analytic continuation requirement and complexity
rubrics_metrics.description: sumnumap(n=a,f,{tab}) uses Abel–Plana and requires f to be holomorphic in the right half-plane Re(z)>a; it evaluates f at O(D log D) real and O(D) complex arguments (D ≈ realprecision·log(10)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geared to slowly decreasing functions; if f decreases exponentially prefer suminf or sumpos. Use sumnumapinit to precompute tables for repeated calls. For Monien-suitable f, sumnummonien may be faster.

rubrics_metrics.name: sumnuminit/sumnumapinit/sumnumlagrangeinit: asymp table initialization format and meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: Initialization functions accept asymp in the form [+oo, alpha]. Positive alpha > 0 encodes exponential decrease exp(−alpha n). Negative alpha with −2 < alpha < −1 encodes polynomial decrease n^{alpha}. sumnumlagrangeinit also accepts parameters describing the remainder expansion (α choices 2,1,1/2,1/3,1/4 or t_CLOSURE g) and an optional c1 controlling interpolation step count.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose asymp according to known tail behaviour; for slow polynomial tails the exact rate must be provided; for exponential tails a rough alpha is sufficient. Initializations can be time-consuming but drastically speed later summations.

rubrics_metrics.name: sumnumlagrange: remainder expansion hypotheses and parameter selection
rubrics_metrics.description: sumnumlagrange(n=a,f,{tab}) uses Lagrange summation assuming the Nth remainder has an asymptotic expansion in integral powers of 1/N by default. The tab can specify alternative expansions via asymp and control interpolation detail via c1. Allowed al values include 1 (default), 1/2, 1/3, 1/4, and 2 (special handling).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selecting incorrect asymp (e.g., wrong β) yields garbage results; examples show ζ(4/3) behaves as n^{-1/3} remainders and requires careful choice of beta/alpha to get correct results. Initialization cost increases for fractional α (1/4 slowest).

rubrics_metrics.name: sumnummonien: Monien summation analytic continuation and defaults
rubrics_metrics.description: sumnummonien(n=a,f,{tab}) assumes f(1/z) has a complex analytic continuation in a neighbourhood of [0,1] and by default that f(n)=O(n^{-2}) with an asymptotic expansion starting at i≥2. It evaluates f at O(D/log D) real arguments (D ≈ realprecision·log(10)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sumnummonieninit to precompute tables for non-standard asymptotic behaviors (asymp, weight w and n0 parameters). The tab supports weights w (log^k or closures) for sums of the form sum f(n) w(n). Ensure consistent n0 across init and subsequent calls. Monien summation can be dramatically faster when its analytic hypotheses hold.

rubrics_metrics.name: sumnummonieninit: asymp and weight parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: sumnummonieninit({asymp},{w},{n0=1}) initializes tables for Monien summation. asymp may be β>0 meaning f(n)=∑ a_i / n^{i+β}, or a vector [α,β] with α>0 and α+β>1 encoding f(n)=∑ a_i / n^{α i+β}. w encodes multiplicative weights (integers k for (log n)^k, closures n->w(n), or [w,fast] variants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select asymp and w to match the summand's analytic structure; otherwise results can be wrong. Precomputation times can be large but subsequent calls are fast.

rubrics_metrics.name: sumnumrat/sumeulerrat/sumeulerrat-like: rational-function summation/product conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions like sumnumrat and sumeulerrat compute sums or Euler-like products when input F is a rational function with degree constraints (e.g., degree ≤ −2 or F−1 rational of degree less than some bound). Poles at integers ≥ a are omitted from summation when specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the input rational function meets the degree/pole hypotheses; these specialized routines give exact or high-precision values for rational-function sums/products when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: sumdiv and sumdivmult: divisor-sum conventions and multiplicativity assumption
rubrics_metrics.description: sumdiv(n,X,expr) sums expr over positive divisors of n; sumdivmult(n,d,expr) sums multiplicative expressions f(d) over divisors d of n and assumes f is multiplicative (f(1)=1 and f(ab)=f(a)f(b) for coprime a,b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If expr is multiplicative use sumdivmult for efficiency. sumdiv wraps a divisors() loop and lexically scopes the loop variable X to the sumdiv call.

rubrics_metrics.name: sumpos: Van Wijngaarden transform for same-sign series and heuristic nature
rubrics_metrics.description: sumpos(X=a,expr,{flag=0}) numerically sums series with same-sign terms using Van Wijngaarden's trick to convert to an alternating series and then applies sumalt. It assumes terms are all of same sign and more or less decreasing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This routine is heuristic and does not check signs; if expr is zero frequently or not truly same-sign results may be wrong. Flag=1 uses the sumalt(,1) variant; space and time complexity are O(p^2) for p digits of accuracy. Use sumalt/suminf according to series structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: representations: number-field structures (nf, bnf, bnr) and contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Number field structures: nf (output of nfinit) contains basic arithmetic data: signature, maximal order basis nf.zk, discriminant, defining polynomial T, etc. bnf (bnfinit) contains nf plus deeper invariants: units U(K), class group Cl(K), and data for discrete log problems. bnr (bnrinit) corresponds to ray class group data and contains bnf plus modulus f and Cl_f(K).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the appropriate initialization (nfinit, bnfinit, bnrinit) according to how much arithmetic/class-field/ray-class data you need. These structures are expected formats for many higher-level routines.

rubrics_metrics.name: algebraic-number input formats and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: An algebraic number in K = Q[X]/(T) may be provided as t_INT, t_FRAC, t_POL (implicitly modulo T), t_POLMOD, or as a t_COL v (dimension N = [K:Q]) giving coordinates in the computed integral basis via sum v[i]*nf.zk[i]. A t_VEC will not be recognized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer t_COL or polynomial/mod representations consistent with the defining polynomial T and nf.zk basis; avoid using t_VEC as it is not accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: ideal representation formats and extended-ideal conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: An ideal may be given as: (i) a principal ideal via an algebraic number in accepted forms, (ii) a prime ideal as the 5-component vector from idealprimedec/idealfactor, (iii) a t_MAT in Hermite Normal Form (HNF) whose columns give a Z-basis, or (iv) an extended ideal [I,t] where I is an ideal and t is an algebraic number representing (t)I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer converting ideals to HNF with idealhnf for functions that expect that format. Extended ideals [I,t] keep track of the principal part t for operations like idealmul/idealsqr/idealinv/idealpow/idealred (which update the principal part); other functions silently discard the extended part (e.g., idealadd).

rubrics_metrics.name: principal part representations and factorizations for extended ideals
rubrics_metrics.description: The principal part t of an extended ideal may be represented as any algebraic number form or as a factorization matrix (in terms of field elements, not ideals), including an empty factorization matrix factor(1) or the empty matrix [;] as synonyms for 1. Many functions accept factored form (famat) inputs to avoid coefficient explosion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When working with giant principal elements, keep them in factorized form to avoid unnecessary expansion; use nffactorback to recover expanded form if needed. Some functions (e.g., ideallog) accept famats directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: finite abelian-group representation and characters
rubrics_metrics.description: A finite abelian group G is represented in user-readable format by its Smith Normal Form as [h,d] or [h,d,g], where h is cardinality, d the vector of elementary divisors and g a vector of generators (G = ⊕ (Z/diZ) g_i). Characters are row vectors χ=[a1,...,an] with χ(∑ g_j n_j) = exp(2π i ∑ a_j n_j/d_j). Subgroups are input as HNF square matrices whose columns express generators in the basis g_i; determinant equals the index (G:H).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this SNF/HNF representation for group computations; ensure elementary divisors satisfy d_n | ... | d_1 and product equals h.

rubrics_metrics.name: relative-extensions and pseudo-matrix conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Relative extensions L/K are represented with rnf (output of rnfinit) where rnf.nf is the base-field nf. A relative matrix is an m×n matrix with entries in K; an ideal list is a row vector of fractional ideals. A pseudo-matrix (A,I) with A a relative matrix and I an ideal list defines a torsion-free projective Z_K-module a1A1 ⊕ ... ⊕ anAn. An integral pseudo-matrix w(A,I,J) requires ai,j ∈ b_i a_j^{-1} for given ideal lists and defines modules and linear maps; arbitrary finite-type Z_K-modules with torsion are given by integral pseudo-matrices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When specifying pseudo- or integral pseudo-matrices follow the ai,j ∈ b_i a_j^{-1} constraint and use the provided data-structure formats; these are required by routines that manipulate projective and torsion Z_K-modules.
